steps.name: Per-sample 20-gene signature score (UCell, singscore check)
caveats: A signature scored on fewer than its 20 genes is a different signature; the reduced size must appear next to the results, not only in a methods footnote
Do not dichotomize the score here — the survival step requires it as a continuous term
steps.context: The signature is supplied by the study as a bare gene-symbol list — not a published marker set — so no external marker database applies. Scoring is rank-based per sample because the downstream Cox model treats the score as a per-subject covariate and must not have it depend on cohort composition. Whether the score separates cases from controls determines how the adjusted Cox coefficient should be interpreted: a score strongly collinear with condition will inflate the standard error of both terms.
steps.question: What is the per-sample score of the study's 20-gene signature in each of the 120 samples, and does the score differ between cases and controls?

grounding.reason: A single unsigned gene list scored per sample: UCell as the rank-based default with singscore as the direction-free cross-check (R-0133); the score tested on the scores with the design and the signature provenance stated (R-0134). preprocessing_scope is stated as a constraint: the gene set is fixed a priori, so no in-fold reselection applies.

constraints: score_method = rank_based_per_sample; input_scale = log_normalized_expression (log2-CPM from T1S2)

preprocessing_scope: the filter and any scaling are fixed by T1S2 and applied to all samples identically; no supervised selection of genes occurs here — the 20 genes are given a priori, which is what keeps the score free of selection bias
Score the signature as a single unsigned set — the file carries no weights and no up/down split; do not invent a direction
Standardize the score to mean 0, SD 1 across the 120 samples and carry both raw and standardized values forward
Report the number of signature genes actually scored beside every score summary
steps.description: Compute a per-sample score for the 20-gene signature on the filtered log2-CPM matrix using UCell (rank-based Mann-Whitney U score, so the score of a sample does not depend on its depth or on the other samples). The signature list has no weights and no direction, so it is scored as a single unsigned up-set. Recompute the same score with singscore as a method-robustness check and report the Spearman correlation between the two score vectors; if the correlation is below 0.8, report both score distributions and carry UCell forward as the primary with the discrepancy stated. Test the score for a case/control difference with a limma model on the scores (one value per sample, so the units are the 120 samples, not the genes) and report the estimate, CI and p. State the signature provenance in the output: source file, 20 symbols requested, number present, method, and input scale.
acceptance_criteria: A per-sample score table for all 120 samples is produced, joined to condition, time and event by sample identifier
UCell and singscore vectors are both computed and their rank correlation is reported
The case-vs-control difference in score is tested on the scores (not the genes) and reported with an effect estimate and CI
Signature provenance is stated: source file, 20 symbols requested, number present in the scored matrix, scoring method, and input scale (log2-CPM)

steps.name: Cox model: signature score vs time-to-event, adjusted for case status
caveats: With 120 subjects the number of events, not the number of samples, bounds the power — if events are few the confidence interval on the hazard ratio will be wide and must be reported as such rather than read as a null

If the score is strongly associated with case/control status (see T2S1), the adjusted score coefficient and the condition coefficient are collinear and both standard errors inflate; report the collinearity diagnostic
.The interaction model splits an already limited event count across arms and is exploratory only
Time-dependent AUC at a horizon beyond the bulk of the follow-up is unstable; choose horizons where the number at risk is reported and non-trivial
steps.context: 120 subjects, 60 cases and 60 controls, one follow-up time and one event indicator per sample. The score is a single pre-specified covariate, not a signature being derived here, so no penalized Cox selection and no cross-validated re-selection is appropriate — that would answer a different question and inflate the apparent performance. The R 'survival' package is absent from this environment; use rms::cph for the Cox fit (rms, riskRegression, pec, timereg, prodlim and survminer are present), or lifelines/scikit-survival on the Python track, and name the package actually used in the output.
steps.question: Is the standardized 20-gene signature score associated with time to the event in this 120-sample cohort after adjusting for case versus control status, and how large is the hazard ratio per standard deviation?

grounding.reason: Association of one per-sample score with a time-to-event outcome: Cox with the clinical covariate, continuous standardized score, HR per SD with CI, Schoenfeld PH check, events/censored/median follow-up stated (R-0153); time-dependent AUC at stated horizons rather than a plain ROC (R-0156); no external cohort, so the in-sample caution is stated (R-0154). Penalized Cox is explicitly not used because the signature is given, not derived.

constraints: The score enters the model as a continuous, standardized term — no median split, no optimized cutpoint before or in place of the test
condition (case vs control) is a covariate in the model; state the reference level explicitly
ph_check = scaled Schoenfeld residuals for all terms
Kaplan-Meier by score tertile is illustration only; no inference is drawn from the tertile split
Do not fit a penalized Cox model to re-derive or re-weight the signature — the 20 genes are given and the question is the association of their score
Name the survival package used; R 'survival' is not installed in this environment
steps.description: Fit a Cox proportional-hazards model of Surv(time, event) on the standardized UCell signature score with condition (case vs control) as a covariate. Report the hazard ratio per one standard deviation of the score with its 95% confidence interval and Wald p-value, alongside the hazard ratio for condition, and report the unadjusted score-only model beside it so the effect of adjustment is visible. The score-by-condition interaction is fitted and reported as a secondary, underpowered analysis
Harrell's C and time-dependent AUC with CIs at explicitly named horizons are reported, together with the number at risk at each horizon
The report states in plain language that all discrimination metrics are in-sample and that no external validation cohort exists for this signature

steps.name: Report and reproducibility record
caveats: A non-significant hazard ratio on a modest event count is an inconclusive result, not evidence of no association — say which one the data supports
steps.context: The deliverable is the answer to one question, not a survey of the data. Everything upstream exists to make the hazard ratio interpretable and to bound how much it should be believed.
steps.question: What does this cohort show about the association between the 20-gene signature score and time to event once case/control status is accounted for, and how strong is that evidence?

grounding.reason: Reproducibility record with sessionInfo, seeds, package versions and the pinned signature source per R-0086.

constraints: Do not restate an exploratory or underpowered result as a conclusion
If the PH assumption failed in T2S2, the report must present the model that was actually valid, not the single hazard ratio
reproducibility_record = session_info, seed, package_versions
steps.description: Assemble a single report: the cohort description (120 samples, 60 cases and 60 controls, events, censored, median follow-up), the QC verdict from T1S1, the gene-filtering and signature-presence audit from T1S2, the score distributions and the case/control score comparison from T2S1, and the Cox results from T2S2 as the answer to the research question. plan.title: 20-gene signature score vs time-to-event, adjusted for case status
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question is a survival association, not a differential expression question: does the per-sample score of the study's 20-gene signature relate to time-to-event once case/control status is in the model? The inputs are a raw Salmon gene-level count matrix (12,000 genes x 120 sample columns plus the gene-symbol column, counts.csv), a 120-row metadata table carrying condition, time and event, and a 20-symbol signature list (signature_genes.csv, one column 'gene', unweighted, so the signature has no up/down direction). Design: 60 cases vs 60 controls, unpaired, single batch, human.

The plan runs four steps in one logical chain. T1S1 does sample-structure QC on the counts (blind VST, PCA on the top 500 variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes, coloured by condition) and reconciles the 120 count columns against the 120 metadata rows — a sample-order or name mismatch between counts.csv and metadata.csv would silently destroy the survival model, so it is checked before anything else. T1S2 filters low-count genes with filterByExpr on the condition grouping, applies TMM scaling factors, and emits a log-CPM matrix; it also reports how many of the 20 signature symbols survive filtering and are present in the matrix at all, because a signature missing genes is a different signature. T2S1 computes the per-sample signature score with UCell (rank-based, so a score does not depend on library depth or on which other samples are in the set), and, as a robustness check that the score is not method-artefact, recomputes it with singscore and reports the correlation between the two; it also tests the score for a case/control difference with limma on the scores, since a score that tracks case status changes how the Cox coefficient must be read. T2S2 is the actual answer: a Cox proportional-hazards model of time/event on the standardized score with condition as a covariate, reporting the hazard ratio per SD with its 95% CI and Wald p, a scaled-Schoenfeld PH check, the score-by-condition interaction as a secondary model (prognostic-within-both-arms vs arm-specific), time-dependent AUC at stated horizons, Harrell's C, and event/censoring counts with median follow-up first. Kaplan-Meier curves by score tertile are drawn as a picture only; no cutpoint enters the inference. T3S1 assembles the report and the reproducibility record.

Deliberately excluded: genome-wide differential expression and enrichment, which the question does not ask for; and any penalized Cox re-derivation of a new signature, since the 20-gene set is given and re-selecting genes on these same samples would produce an optimistic, uninterpretable estimate. The plan carries one hard caveat throughout — the signature is scored and tested on the same cohort with no external validation, so every performance number (C-index, time-dependent AUC) is in-sample and must be reported as such. Note also that the R 'survival' package is not in the environment; the Cox fit uses rms::cph (with riskRegression/pec/timereg present as alternatives), and survminer is available for the KM picture.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes
TMM normalization (edgeR) then log-CPM for scoring
UCell rank-based signature scores per sample
Cox proportional hazards model on the 20-gene signature score with condition as covariate

steps.name: Report and reproducibility record
steps.question: What does this cohort show about the association between the 20-gene signature score and time to event once case/control status is accounted for, and how strong is that evidence?
steps.description: Assemble a single report: the cohort description (120 samples, 60 cases and 60 controls, events, censored, median follow-up), the QC verdict from T1S1, the gene-filtering and signature-presence audit from T1S2, the score distributions and the case/control score comparison from T2S1, and the Cox results from T2S2 as the answer to the research question. Lead with the adjusted hazard ratio per SD and its confidence interval, then the evidence around it. State explicitly what the analysis does not establish: no external validation, no causal claim, discrimination metrics in-sample, and the interaction test exploratory. Attach the reproducibility record — sessionInfo, package versions, random seeds for any resampling, and the exact signature file and number of genes scored.
steps.context: The deliverable is the answer to one question, not a survey of the data. Everything upstream exists to make the hazard ratio interpretable and to bound how much it should be believed.
acceptance_criteria: The report leads with the adjusted hazard ratio per SD of the signature score with its CI and p-value
Event counts, median follow-up, and the number of the 20 signature genes actually scored appear in the main text, not only in a supplement
Limitations are stated explicitly: single cohort, no external validation, in-sample discrimination, exploratory interaction
A reproducibility record with sessionInfo, package versions and seeds is stored with the results
constraints: Do not restate an exploratory or underpowered result as a conclusion
If the PH assumption failed in T2S2, the report must present the model that was actually valid, not the single hazard ratio

caveats: A non-significant hazard ratio on a modest event count is an inconclusive result, not evidence of no association — say which one the data supports
